title: The Man Who Drilled Under His Own Seat
text:
The rabbinic collection Leviticus Rabbah preserves a short parable taught in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai.

Some people were sitting together in a boat, out on the water. One of them took a drill and began boring a hole in the floor under his own seat.

The others stared at him. What are you doing? they asked.

What business is it of yours? he answered. Am I not drilling under my own place?

They replied that it was very much their business. When the water came up through his hole, it would not stay under his seat. It would flood the boat for all of them.

The rabbis used the parable to explain how one person's wrongdoing affects a whole community. The passage applies it to a verse from the Book of Job, where Job's friend complains that Job's error does not stay with him alone. A community is like that boat: what one member does to his own corner, everyone else will share.
lesson: In a shared enterprise, no one's choices are purely private. Speak up early when someone's action threatens the whole boat, even if it looks like his own business.
people: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, passengers on a boat
